producer_report.summary: The steward now decides for itself and asks the owner only about an environment change or a token or credential, and code enforces that routing by the brief's presence. decide() never applies a change that carries a brief. It records it as a proposal with its brief at any rung, whatever its kind. A change without a brief is applied inside the limit and only recorded above it, with brief None. open_proposals lists an undecided proposal that has a brief, or that has none and whose raising role may change its rung (the drain approves those, and the audience role's items rely on that). in_limit is false for a briefed item. The decisions page (xtask needs_owner) uses the same test. A new blind_spot_needing_owner gives a missing-token source a brief, kind proposal, the source as evidence and the key blind-spot:github:owner-action, so an earlier plain blind-spot:github does not hide it. validate_items needs a request for an in-limit item only when it has no brief. STEWARD_PROMPT is rewritten (step back, decide yourself, brief only for env/token, owner action in if_yes). The role is version 3 (steward-3.json). The output-schema descriptions in outputs.rs say the same. A new test composes the real prompt with the contract and asserts at most 600 estimated tokens. The docs, CHANGELOG and D169 mark the prompt and schema wording prose-only and the routing code-enforced. The user prompt in steward.rs brief() was reworded to match.

open_issues: Departure from the plan's file list, as the plan itself allowed: I edited four files outside the listed deliverables, namely crates/athena-context/src/outputs.rs (descriptions and one test), xtask/src/decisions.rs (needs_owner and its tests), and fixture-only briefs in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs and crates/athena-cli/tests/work_decisions.rs. Without them the owner page would still route by rung, the model-facing schema would still say to brief every over-limit proposal, and criteria 1 and 6 could not both hold.

An unbriefed item above the limit is recorded, but its key stays in the seen set. It is found only in the records or by its id, and it is not raised again. An applied in-limit proposal still has no decision recorded, so the drain could approve it a second time. This was already so at base. Both are named in D169 and the design doc.
No code checks that a brief is about an environment or token need. This is prose-only and out of scope.
The next steward run commits a version-3 role record, as designed.
I did not measure the exact composed token count of the real prompt. The test asserts at most 600 under the ceil(bytes/3) estimate, and it passes.
mistakes: My first context test used jiff::Timestamp, which athena-context does not depend on. I fixed it with a string parse.

Several older steward.rs tests used a default item/change helper that carries a brief. After the routing change they would have been recorded as Proposed and not Applied. I found them when the tests failed and set brief None in each.
learnings: The producer's tool policy denies tail, sed, cat and compound or substituted commands. Cargo output cannot be filtered, so -q helps.
A cargo build-slot lock makes a second cargo run in the same job wait up to 300 s and exit with code 75 while a background cargo run holds the slot. Retrying works.
athena-context has no jiff dependency, so its tests build a timestamp with a string .parse().unwrap().

The schema doc comments on StewardItemOutput.brief and StewardBriefOutput are the text the model reads for the brief. They said 'required for a proposal above your limit' and had to be reworded with the prompt.
open_proposals, find_open and the xtask page filter on WorkItemKind::Proposal, so an owner-bound item of another kind must be recorded as a Proposal to be seen.
desires: A way to filter cargo output (a tail or grep on a pipe) would make the verbose test logs easier to check.
A readable path to the background task's output file, to see per-test results of the full suite.
